subject: TruHealth capacity comparison and delivery path: private vs dedicated
messages:
From: Dr. Priya Nair <priya.nair@truhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jason Lee <jason.lee@cloudbuyer.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing ask for regulated AI hosting

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for walking us through the demo last week. As discussed with procurement, TruHealth is evaluating two hosting paths for our clinical assistant pilot: a Redwood-hosted Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs in your cloud) versus a Private deployment in our VPC (customer-managed fleet). We need a firm capacity estimate for both options tied to our pilot KPIs so procurement can lock down budget for Q3.

Quick background: 3k clinicians, pilot scope is narrow (medication reconciliation, note summarization) with peak expected concurrency of ~90 concurrent active sessions and median prompt+response length ~450 tokens. Target P50 latency <300ms for chat completions and 99th <=900ms. Expected pilot throughput ~1M tokens/day ramping to 2.5M tokens/day over 8 weeks.

Can you provide: 1) GPU count and type recommendation for Dedicated vs Private; 2) approximate monthly OPEX/cost buckets (in USD) for both options; 3) compliance gaps we should expect to own for Private; 4) an ETA to get pilot live (provisioning + onboarding).

We attached our procurement template and a short SOC2 questionnaire. Procurement is on a tight timeline — would like a summary by EOD Friday.

Best,
Priya
Director, Clinical Informatics
TruHealth Systems

Attachments: procurement_template.xlsx, TruHealth_SOC2_questions.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Priya Nair <priya.nair@truhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask for regulated AI hosting

Priya — thanks for the clear brief. Looping in Laura and Rishi to cover Dedicated capacity economics and Private deployment details. High level answers below; I attached a short workbook with slides and the capacity sheet (truhealth_isolation_capacity_workbook.xlsx). I can update the numbers after any changes to traffic assumptions.

Summary (pilot: 90 concurrent, P50<300ms, ~1–2.5M tokens/day):

- Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved pool)
  - Recommendation: 8 x NVIDIA H100 80GB (reserved), with 2x standby GPUs for burst/canary -> effective pool of 10 for reliability.
  - Rationale: H100 gives headroom for larger-context models (16k) and better perf per token for our evals. Continuous batching and prefix caching on Redwood reduces token cost.
  - Expected perf: ~P50=220–320ms depending on model and sequence; 99th typically 700–950ms with proper batching and autoscale configs.
  - Monthly run-rate (OPEX): estimated $78k–$95k (includes reserved capacity amortized, networking, storage, basic observability). Pricing varies with term (12 vs 36 months) and committed utilization.
  - Onboarding ETA: provisioned in 7–10 business days (account + routing + canary).

- Private (VPC customer-managed)
  - Recommendation (on-prem or customer cloud): 12 x NVIDIA H100 80GB nodes (or 18 x A100 80GB if Tegra procurement latency is an issue) + 2 management nodes.
  - Rationale: Private adds overhead for patching, KMS, and audit logging; need additional capacity to absorb lower shared-efficiency (no multi-tenant batching across customers) and extra redundancy for maintenance windows.
  - Expected perf: P50 similar in ideal config but variance increases; 99th may rise to 1.0–1.5s depending on network egress and infra tuning.
  - Upfront CAPEX + integration services: one-time ~ $640k–$820k depending on hardware and install; monthly ops (monitoring, backups, support) add ~$18k–$26k.
  - Onboarding ETA: 6–10 weeks (hardware lead times, network/VPC setup, KMS integration, SOC/controls verification).

Compliance and operational notes:
- Private: TruHealth owns the SC-08 control path (customer-managed identity and network segmentation). Redwood provides audit-log integrations, an audited control-plane connector, and a SOC2 playbook. Expect 2–3 weeks of audit evidence collection.
- Dedicated: Redwood-managed control plane reduces TruHealth scope; we provide SOC2 report, encryption in-transit and at-rest, and optional VPC peering for restricted traffic flows.

Open items required from TruHealth to firm numbers:
1) Target models (open vs fine-tuned proprietary model) — size differs substantially.
2) Required data residency boundaries for Private (region/availability-zone constraints).
3) Peak concurrency confirmation and planned ramp schedule (week-by-week).

Next steps: Laura — can you validate the cost buckets and add a short canary run proposal? Rishi — can you prepare an itemized gap list for the SOC2 items TruHealth flagged? Priya — if you can share the target model name (or confirm ref model) and a signed NDA (if needed), we’ll finalize the sheet by Friday EOD.

Thanks — Karthik
Head of Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: truhealth_isolation_capacity_workbook.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dr. Priya Nair <priya.nair@truhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask for regulated AI hosting

Priya / team — added comments to the workbook and appended a short canary plan. Key callouts:

- TCO sensitivity: if TruHealth plans heavy fine-tuning or long-context (>8k), shift to +25–40% GPU count. The workbook contains an alternate column labelled "FT / LongCtx" with those numbers.
- Canary plan: 2-week canary on Dedicated (2 H100s) with traffic mirroring from prod API to validate latency and egress flows. Canary cost estimate: ~$8k–$12k.
- Fallback: we recommend a hybrid approach for the pilot — start on Dedicated with a Private runbook (playbook + IaC) prepared in parallel. That lets you hit Q3 timelines while preserving Private as a compliance final-state if required.

Pricing detail (rough breakout):
- Dedicated: hardware amortization 55%, infra ops 20%, licensing/observability 15%, support 10%.
- Private: hardware 70%, integration services 15%, ongoing ops 15% (higher because TruHealth likely needs a runbook + training).

I've also attached our SOC2 checklist and a one-pager on Private vs Dedicated controls (SOC2-Audit-Checklist.pdf, redwood_private_vs_dedicated_onepager.pdf). Rishi — ready for the SOC items. Monica — can you draft the canary runbook and include rollback gates?

Laura Bennett
Head of Solutions — Redwood Console

Attachments: redwood_private_vs_dedicated_onepager.pdf, SOC2-Audit-Checklist.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Priya Nair <priya.nair@truhealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 16:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask for regulated AI hosting

Priya — attaching an itemized SOC2 gap list and an evidence checklist I promised. Short summary: Dedicated covers ~70% of TruHealth's controls out-of-the-box (encryption, incident response, logging). Private requires additional attestations around change management, HSM/KMS proofing, and on-prem network segmentation.

Deliverables we can provide by Tuesday:
- Evidence pack for Dedicated (SOC2 PDF, encryption certs, network diagrams)
- Gap list and recommended remediation timeline for Private (2–4 weeks of work to reach parity depending on TruHealth's infra readiness)

If TruHealth confirms model choice (recommend starting with open-refactor-large-v1), we will re-run perf estimates and finalize the worksheet.

I'll follow up with a shared Drive link to the evidence pack and a DocuSign MSA placeholder (if procurement wants to parallelize).

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Security & Compliance Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2-evidence-pkg.zip, private_deployment_gaplist.xlsx
